title: On-call and Incident Response Playbook
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Summary
This document defines Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response processes, runbook expectations, postmortem requirements, rotation policies, game day guidance, and templates for status page and customer communications. It is the canonical operational playbook for production incidents affecting availability, correctness, performance, and data integrity.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Provide a reproducible, low-friction process that keeps customer-facing systems healthy, minimizes customer impact, and surfaces actionable follow-ups.
- Scope: Applies to all production-facing services (e.g., inference-runtime, routing-service, kv-cache, batching-engine, control-plane) across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Audience: On-call engineers, incident commanders, SREs, tech leads, support leads, and product managers.

Incident lifecycle (high level)
1. Detection and triage
   - Alert received via PagerDuty -> Slack channel #oncall-alerts -> incident creation in Incident Manager (Jira/StatusPage ticket).
   - Initial triage window: 5 minutes for P0/P1 alerts, 15 minutes for P2.
2. Declare incident and assign roles
   - Incident Commander (IC) declared within 10 minutes for P0/P1.
   - Roles assigned: IC, Communication Lead, Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), Support Liaison, and Postmortem owner.
3. Mitigation and containment
   - Follow runbook playbooks (see Runbooks section) for immediate mitigation (fallback routing, scale-up, model-variant failover, cache invalidation).
4. Recovery and verification
   - Restore user-facing functionality to acceptable SLO thresholds and verify with synthetic checks and customer-facing tests.
5. Communication
   - Internal updates every 15 minutes for P0/P1 until resolution; external status updates as per Status Page cadence below.
6. Post-incident
   - Postmortem created within 48 hours (draft) and finalized within 7 days. Action items assigned and tracked.

Severity definitions and SLOs
- P0: Complete outage or critical degradation for multiple customers or all traffic (e.g., control plane unavailable, inference-runtime crash loop). Response: immediate, IC within 10 minutes. Target MTTR <1 hour for common failure classes.
- P1: Severe degradation affecting significant subset of customers (high latency spikes >5x baseline, heavy error rates). Response: IC within 30 minutes. Target MTTR <4 hours.
- P2: Partial impact or single-customer degradation. Response: acknowledge within 60 minutes. Target MTTR <24 hours.
- P3: Informational, low-impact issues or non-urgent infra work.
Key SLO thresholds (examples):
- Hosting API availability: 99.95% monthly (measured at the gateway).
- Generation P99 latency (small payload): <= 250ms for hosted tier under normal load.
- Error rate: <0.3% 5xx across all API endpoints.
- Embeddings throughput SLOs documented per model in model-catalog runbooks.

Roles and responsibilities
- Incident Commander (IC): Owns the incident, coordinates mitigation, declares severity, and approves communications.
- Communication Lead: Drafts and publishes internal and external updates (Status Page, email templates).
- SMEs: Execute technical mitigations, interpret telemetry, and update IC.
- Support Liaison: Surfacing customer impact, mapping affected customers, and coordinating escalations with sales/CS.
- Postmortem Owner: Drafts the timeline, root cause analysis (RCA), and action items.

Escalation policy
- Primary on-call engineer receives initial alert. If not acknowledged in 3 minutes for P0/P1, escalate to secondary within PagerDuty. If still unacknowledged after 5 minutes, escalate to team lead and SRE manager.
- For P0 incidents, page engineering director after 15 minutes if unresolved.

Runbooks: structure and mandatory fields
Every production service must have a runbook in the canonical runbooks repo (confluence path: eng-platform/runbooks). Runbook schema (plain-text template fields required):
- title (short descriptive name)
- service (service owning the runbook)
- owner (pager/team)
- severity triggers (alerts/metrics thresholds that map to P0/P1/P2)
- immediate actions (1-5 step checklist for first 15 minutes)
- rollback or failover steps
- verification checks (synthetic and customer-facing)
- side effects and mitigation risks
- post-incident actions (what to capture in the postmortem)

Example immediate actions (inference-runtime high error rate):
1. Capture current error rate and recent deploys: `kubectl get deploys --namespace inference` and check recent CI/CD merge.
2. Scale up inference pods by 50%: `kubectl scale deployment inference-runtime --replicas=<current*1.5>`.
3. Toggle model-variant fallback: set routing-service flag `use_fallback=true`.
4. If errors persist, revert last model/serving-config change via control-plane rollback.

On-call rotations and coverage
- Teams must publish rotation schedules in the team wiki and PagerDuty.
- Primary responsibilities: 24/7 coverage for P0/P1, with secondary and tertiary backups. Daytime shifts (08:00-20:00 local) have rapid escalation; overnight shifts rely on on-call rotation with longer escalation windows.
- Shift length: typical rotations are 1 week for engineering on-call. Follow local labor laws for limits; teams may opt for shorter handoffs (48-72 hours) for high-burn periods.
- Handover checklist for shift change:
  1. Confirm no active incidents and all queues are acknowledged.
  2. Review open P1/P2 tickets and action items.
  3. Run a short sanity check: verify synthetic checks, recent deploy health, and major customer alerts.

Game days and drills
- Purpose: Validate runbooks, verify tooling, rehearse communication cadence, and measure MTTR.
- Quarterly game days per team; company-wide game days twice per year.
- Example drills: region failure (simulate region scale-down), model-variant regression (deploy a degraded model to canary), control-plane outage (disable control-plane reads).
- Success criteria: Runbook execution time within expected windows, postmortem produced, and follow-up actions assigned.

Postmortem process and quality criteria
- Timeline: Draft due within 48 hours; final postmortem with action items and owners due within 7 days.
- Required sections: executive summary, timeline, root cause analysis, impact (customer and internal metrics), action items (owner + due date), prevention plan, and lessons learned.
- Blameless culture: Focus on systemic fixes and process improvements. Avoid individual blame.
- Severity-based depth: P0 and high-visibility P1 incidents require a deeper RCA with instrumentation artifacts (logs, traces, metrics) and testable prevention items.

Status page and external communications templates
- Status page URL: https://status.redwood-inference.example.com
- Status cadence: initial public post within 30 minutes for P0 affecting >10% customers or P1 affecting multiple large customers. Update frequency: every 30 minutes while active, then every 2-4 hours as stabilized.

Public status update template (short):
- Title: [Identified] Major API Degradation — Generation Errors
- Impact: Customers may see 5xx errors or increased latency for text generation requests.
- Next update: in 30 minutes or sooner.
- Mitigation: We have routed traffic to fallback model variants and increased capacity in affected clusters.
- Public link: https://status.redwood-inference.example.com/incidents/1234

Customer email template (for account-level impact):
- Subject: Incident affecting Redwood Inference service on <date> — <brief impact>
- Body: Hello <CustomerName>,
  We experienced an incident between <start time> and <end time> that impacted <affected feature>. We have routed around the issue and restored normal operation by <time>. Actions taken: <short list>. Next steps: <follow-up commit/compensation/contact>. We will share a postmortem by <date>.
  Thank you for your patience,
  Support Team, Redwood Inference

Internal communication cadence and templates
- Internal update every 15 minutes for P0/P1:
  - Subject: [INCIDENT] <short title> — <progress/next steps>
  - Body: Current status, mitigation steps taken, next actions, owner list, ETA for next update.

Tools and integrations
- PagerDuty: primary paging and escalation.
- Slack: #oncall-alerts for automated alerts, #incident-<id> created per incident for coordination.
- StatusPage: public incident publishing.
- Jira/Issue Tracker: create incident ticket and link to postmortem.
- Datadog / Grafana / Tempo: metrics, dashboards, and traces for RCA.
- CI/CD rollback playbooks integrated with control-plane API for safe rollback.

Operational runbook hygiene
- Ownership: Team must review runbooks quarterly and after any relevant incident or deploy change.
- Runbook tests: Runbooks must include a 'dry-run' checklist and be exercised during team game days.
- Naming convention: `runbook/<service>/<short-name>` and include last-reviewed date in header.

Governance and metrics
- On-call burn metrics tracked monthly: alerts per shift, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to recover (MTTR), and number of rollbacks.
- SLA/SLO misses must trigger a review with product and reliability teams and be included in QBRs.

Appendix: quick templates and example commands
- Example status page short update: "We are investigating increased 5xx errors for text-generation endpoints. Our engineers are actively working on a mitigation. Next update in 30 minutes."
- Example rollback command (control-plane API): `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/rollback -d '{\"service\":\"inference-runtime\",\"to_revision\":\"2026.02.01-rc\"}'`
- Example verification query to check synthetic readiness:
  - `curl -s https://gateway.redwood.example.com/healthz | jq .`
  - `wrk -t2 -c50 -d30s https://gateway.redwood.example.com/generate?model=gptx-small`

Related docs and runbooks
- eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets (SLO definitions and alert thresholds)
- eng-platform/runbooks (canonical runbook repo)
- eng-infra/incident-review (postmortem and RCA templates)

Owners and maintenance
- Playbook owner: Eng SRE (primary contact: Marcus Lee).
- Review cadence: This playbook is reviewed annually and after every Sev0/Sev1 incident.
- Feedback: For improvements, file a PR against this Confluence page or contact the Eng SRE team.

Document history
- 2024-06-12: Created by Aisha Kapoor.
- 2025-10-21: Updated game-day frequency and SLO examples.
- 2026-02-10: Reviewed and updated templates, escalation windows, and runbook schema.
